x.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
This is correct. The vast majority of enterprise workflows have not actually had agents applied to them in any meaningful way. The economy probably has this deployed < 1% right now.

At best you have a few automated systems in a company that do a single pass of an LLM to make a decision or provide feedback, but very little real “automation”. Some of this is a statement about the adoption rates of technology in enterprises, but the vast majority of it is really just due to the capability of AI itself.

That’s all changing. Now with computer use, long running agents, harness improvements and surrounding infrastructure, we’re finally at a point where we can start to apply agents at more complex workflows. 

We will see self-improving systems that can take any particular workflow goal and improve the execution rates over a volume of instances. And with the emerging form factor of agent swarms, you can just choose to deploy any amount of compute at a problem and agents will off and do the work.

This won’t be about and users prompting agents to complete a specific task for them, but instead the organization reengineering the underlying workflows to take advantage of agents in their processes. This will have a massive impact in finance, life sciences, healthcare, and other information-heavy domains. Lots of opportunity to build and deploy these systems right now.

tweets.text:
the hex team consistently gets what it means to build agents, and software to support them

three things that caught my eye from Hex 4.0 that mirror what we've done at LangChain and that I think speak to the future of building agents

1/ use code as a backbone. they moved from yaml to more flexible code. agents are really good at writing code, and people want lots of flexibility in UI, so i think we will see more teams have parts of their UI that are powered by code. We did this in LangSmith with Custom Apps (completely custom UI)

2/ UX focused on reviewing. "A new, intuitive Hex UI, built for reviewing and understanding". As agents do more work, the bottleneck becomes reviewing work. We did a similar thing in LangSmith with our new Trajectory view, focused on being a new view over agent trajectories that make it easy to review

3/ rebuilt core infra. "An all-new, ridiculously faster execution engine". agents will still use infra/software. and it will need to be faster/better to accomodate more usage. We did this in LangSmith with SmithDB, our custom database for agent traces

I think all these three things (lets agents write custom UIs as code, invest in UI/UX that make it easier to review, make your core infra more scalable) are all generalizable to any company building agents

congrats to Hex team on a great milestone and great launch!

> How plans work

All plans give you access to every model. Your choice of model and the size of your tasks affect how quickly you use your allowance.

Daily and weekly limits apply, along with a monthly allowance. You can see how much you've used and when each limit resets on the Usage page.

More expensive models have an additional monthly limit; which models count depends on your plan. If you reach it, you can keep using other models within your remaining allowance.

If you use up your included usage, you can switch to an available free model, wait for your allowance to reset, or continue with purchased pay-as-you-go credits.

> FAQS

How much more usage do Super and Ultra include?

Super gives you substantially more included usage than Plus, and Ultra more again. Each plan card above lists its included Cloud agent size. How much work you can do depends on the models you choose and the size of your tasks.

What counts toward usage?

Model and included tool usage in Hermes Agent count toward your allowance when you sign in with your Nous account. Hosting for one Cloud agent is included as well. API-key requests and additional Cloud agents use pay-as-you-go credits.

When does my usage reset?

Daily usage resets after 24 hours, and weekly usage after seven days, starting when you first use each window. Your monthly allowance and large-model allowance reset with your billing period. Your Usage page shows the exact reset times.

These limits apply together: a daily reset won't restore included usage if you've reached your weekly or monthly limit.

What happens when I reach a limit?

You can wait for the reset or switch to an available free model. Turn on Keep going on credits to continue using paid models with your pay-as-you-go balance. Leave it off and Hermes won't spend those credits when your included usage runs out.

If you reach only the large-model limit, other models remain available within your remaining allowance.

What happens to my existing subscription?

When you switch, unused subscription credits carry over as pay-as-you-go credits, up to one month of your current plan's credits. Switching to a plan at the same price takes effect immediately with nothing to pay that day. Upgrades charge the price difference; downgrades take effect at the end of your billing period.

Once you switch, you can't return to a legacy paid plan.

We've revamped Hermes Agent subscriptions. 

Every new plan now includes a cloud agent out of the box, and usage has daily and weekly limits instead of one monthly block of credits.

Subscribers can switch to the new plans any time at https://t.co/hsnPi9hDPn https://t.co/t4fl3FrxQv
